example.message: Bad request - Resource should have a name

CpuCoreLimit.description: Limitations on the number of CPUs consumed by the workload (0.5, 1, .etc). The system guarantees that this workload will not be able to consume more than this amount of CPUs.

CpuCoreRequest.description: CPU units to allocate for the created workload (0.5, 1, .etc). The workload will receive at least this amount of CPU. Note that the workload will not be scheduled unless the system can guarantee this amount of CPUs to the workload.

CpuMemoryLimit.description: Limitations on the CPU memory to allocate for this workload (1G, 20M, .etc). The system guarantees that this workload will not be able to consume more than this amount of memory. The workload will receive an error when trying to allocate more memory than this limit.

CpuMemoryRequest.description: The amount of CPU memory to allocate for this workload (1G, 20M, .etc). The workload will receive at least this amount of memory. Note that the workload will not be scheduled unless the system can guarantee this amount of memory to the workload

resource.description: The name of the extended resource (mandatory)

quantity.description: The requested quantity for the resource.

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the extended resource is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

GpuComputeMode.description: GPU compute sharing mode. Policy and template defaults apply before the built-in time-slicing fallback. Explicit modes require Run:ai cluster version 3.0.14 or later.

GpuDevicesRequest.description: Requested number of GPU devices. Currently if more than one device is requested, it is not possible to provide values for gpuMemory or gpuPortion.

GpuMemoryLimit.description: Limitation on the memory consumed by the workload, per GPU device. The system guarantees The gpuMemoryLimit must be no less than gpuMemoryRequest.

GpuMemoryPortionLimit.description: Maximum GPU memory fraction consumed per GPU device. Must be no less than gpuMemoryPortionRequest.

GpuMemoryPortionRequest.description: GPU memory fraction to allocate per GPU device, between 0 and 1. Required when gpuRequestType is portion.

GpuMemoryRequest.description: Required if and only if gpuRequestType is memory. States the GPU memory to allocate for the created workload, per GPU device. Note that the workload will not be scheduled unless the system can guarantee this amount of GPU memory to the workload.

GpuPortionLimit.description: Deprecated. Use gpuMemoryPortionLimit instead. Limitations on the portion consumed by the workload, per GPU device. The system guarantees The gpuPotionLimit must be no less than the gpuPortionRequest.

GpuPortionRequest.description: Deprecated. Use gpuMemoryPortionRequest instead. Required if and only if gpuRequestType is portion. States the portion of the GPU to allocate for the created workload, per GPU device, between 0 and 1. The default is no allocated GPUs.

GpuRequestType.description: Sets the unit type for GPU resources requests. Stated in terms of portion or memory. Sets the unit type for other GPU request fields. If `gpuDevicesRequest > 1`, only `portion` is supported. If `gpuDeviceRequest = 1`, the request type can be stated as `portion` or `memory`.

LargeShmRequest.description: A large /dev/shm device to mount into a container running the created workload. An shm is a shared file system mounted on RAM.

K8sObjectMeta.description: Metadata of the Kubernetes resource that is created by this k8sObject

annotations.description:
Free-form annotations attached to the resource. Keys must conform
to Kubernetes qualified-name syntax
(https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations/#syntax-and-character-set):
an optional DNS-subdomain prefix (≤253 chars) followed by "/" and a
required name component ([A-Za-z0-9] with `.`, `_`, `-` allowed
inside, ≤63 chars). Key syntax is enforced at runtime on both
create and update; annotation values have no format constraint
beyond the length limit below.

labels.description:
Free-form labels attached to the resource. Keys and values must
conform to Kubernetes label syntax
(https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/#syntax-and-character-set):
keys are qualified names (optional DNS-subdomain prefix ≤253 chars
+ "/" + name component ≤63 chars); values are ≤63 chars matching
the same [A-Za-z0-9]/`.`/`_`/`-` character set (empty values are
allowed). Key syntax is validated at runtime; the value pattern
below is enforced by the schema as well as at runtime.

K8sObjectSpec.description:
Common shape for k8s-object asset specs: the raw Kubernetes object
metadata (labels/annotations) and the raw Kubernetes object spec.
Shared between the k8s-object CRUD APIs (e.g. RctSpec) and the
cluster-facing k8s-objects sync API (K8sObjectsUpdate).

objectSpec.description: The raw Kubernetes spec of the object.

ScopeId.description: The id of the cluster, department or project, depending on the scope type.

next.description: Offset for the next page of results. Present only when there are more entries beyond the current page (i.e., the number of returned entries equals the limit).

ReportedWorkloadType.description: The type of the workload. Any workload type the cluster reports, not only the NVIDIA Run:ai native ones.

name.description: Pod-local name of the claim entry, as listed in `pod.spec.resourceClaims[].name` and referenced by containers in `resources.claims`.

claimName.description: Name of the ResourceClaim bound to the pod for this entry. For a claim generated from a template, this is null until Kubernetes creates and binds the claim.

resourceClaims.description: The pod's claims that were generated from the resource claim template. A pod usually has one, but may list several when more than one of its claim entries references the same template.

pods.description: The pods of the workload that reference the resource claim template.

next.description: Offset for the next page of results. Present only when there are more workloads beyond the current page (i.e., the number of returned workloads equals the limit).

workloads.description: The workloads whose pods currently reference the resource claim template.

ClusterSyncReportUpdate.description: success/failure report of a single update attempt of the cluster

id.description: a unique id of the entity being updated (asset, workload, policy, etc).

updateAttemptTime.description: the time in which the cluster attempted the update.

message.description: optional failure message for the case that the update has failed. should be sent null if the update was successful.

ClusterSyncReport.description: allow cluster to report about success/failures of sync updates

RequestInfo.description: value that the agent sent to the afterUpdate query parameter.

ResponseInfo.description: The lowest and highest update counts included in this bulk of updates. for example, it is possible that agent requester for afterUpdate=10 and received a bulk of four updates - 12, 13, 16, 18. in this case lowestUpdate=12, highestUpdate=18.

SystemInfo.description: the highest update count that was assigned to the data being synchronized. for example, it is possible that the agent sent afterUpdate=12 and received a bulk containing only four updates (13, 15, 18, 19) but in the system there is already update 21 which was not included in this bulk and can be received in the following bulk.

secretAccessKey.description: The secret access key of the S3-compatible bucket, required only when not using existing secret.

keyId.description: id of the encryption key which has been used to encrypt an asset's data.

existingSecretName.description: optional name of existing secret in the cluster from which the user name and password should be taken. user.description: The name of the user, required only when not using existing secret.

password.description: The password, required only when not using existing secret.

If omitted, you will have to provide those credentials and url in relevant fields. user.description: The name of the user, required only when not using existing secret.

password.description: The password, required only when not using existing secret.

url.description: The url, required only when not using existing secret.

KeyValuePair.description: Details of key-value pair to be stored in the credential.

GenericSecretKeyValuePairs.description: Set of key-value pairs to store in the new credential.

existingSecretName.description: name of existing secret in the cluster from which the general key-value values should be taken.

name.description: The name of the resource created for the asset in the cluster.

ClusterInfo.description: Cluster related information of the asset.

Args.description: Arguments to the command that the container running the workload executes.

Command.description: A command to the server as the entry point of the container running the workload.

EnvironmentVariableCredential.description: Details of the secret and key use to populate the environment variable. (mutually exclusive with value)

key.description: The key in the secret resource. (mandatory)

EnvironmentVariableConfigMap.description: Details of the configMap and key use to populate the environment variable

name.description: The name of the config-map resource. (mandatory)

key.description: The key in the config-map resource. (mandatory)

EnvironmentVariablePodFieldReference.description: Details of the field-reference and key use to populate the environment variable

EnvironmentVariableOfAsset.description: Details of an environment variable which is populated into the container.

name.description: The name of the environment variable. (mandatory)

value.description: The value of the environment variable. (mutually exclusive with credential, configMap and podFieldRef)

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the environment variable is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

EnvironmentVariablesOfAsset.description: Set of environment variables to populate into the container running the workspace.

RunAsGid.description: The group id to run the entrypoint of the container which executes the workspace. Default to the value specified in the environment asset `runAsGid` field (optional). Use only when the source uid/gid of the environment asset is not `fromTheImage`, and `overrideUidGidInWorkspace` is enabled.

RunAsUid.description: The user id to run the entrypoint of the container which executes the workspace. Default to the value specified in the environment asset `runAsUid` field (optional). Use only when the source uid/gid of the environment asset is not `fromTheImage`, and `overrideUidGidInWorkspace` is enabled.

SupplementalGroups.description: Comma separated list of groups that the user running the container belongs to, in addition to the group indicated by runAsGid. Use only when the source uid/gid of the environment asset is not `fromTheImage`, and `overrideUidGidInWorkspace` is enabled. Using an empty string implies reverting the supplementary groups of the image.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation.description: Allow the container running the workload and all launched processes to gain additional privileges after the workload starts. For more information consult the [User Identity in Container guide](/run-ai/self-hosted/documentation/installation-and-configuration/configuration/security/user-identity-in-containers)

Capabilities.description: Add POSIX capabilities to running containers. Defaults to the default set of capabilities granted by the container runtime.

CreateHomeDir.description: When set to `true`, creates a home directory for the container.

HostIpc.description: Whether to enable host IPC. Defaults to false.

HostNetwork.description: Whether to enable host networking. Default to false.

Image.description: Docker image name. For more information, see [Images](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images). The image name is mandatory for creating a workload.

ImagePullPolicy.description: Image pull policy. Defaults to `Always` if `:latest` tag is specified, otherwise it is `IfNotPresent`.

ProbeHandlerScheme.description: Scheme to use for connecting to the host, defaults to HTTP.

ProbeHandler.description: The action taken to determine the health of the container. (mandatory)

httpGet.description: An action based on HTTP Get requests.

path.description: Path to access on the HTTP server, defaults to /.

port.description: Number of the port to access on the container.

host.description: Host name to connect to, defaults to the pod IP.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness or readiness probes are initiated.

periodSeconds.description: How often (in seconds) to perform the probe.

timeoutSeconds.description: Number of seconds after which the probe times out.

successThreshold.description: Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed.

failureThreshold.description: When a probe fails, the number of times to try before giving up.

Probes.description: Probes are used to determine if the container is healthy and ready to accept traffic.

ReadOnlyRootFileSystem.description: If true, mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only.

RunAsNonRoot.description: Force the container to run as a non-root user.

SeccompProfileType.description: Indicates which kind of seccomp profile will be applied to the container. The options are a. `RuntimeDefault` - the container runtime default profile should be used. b. `Unconfined` - no profile should be applied. c. `Localhost` is not yet supported by Run:ai.

Stdin.description: Whether this container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime. If this is not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF

Tty.description: Whether this container should allocate a TTY for itself, also requires 'stdin' to be true.

UidGidSource.description: Indicate the way to determine the user and group ids of the container. The options are a. `fromTheImage` - user and group ids are determined by the docker image that the container runs. this is the default option. b. `custom` - user and group ids can be specified in the environment asset and/or the workload creation request. c. `idpToken` - user and group IDs are automatically taken from the identity provider (IdP) token (available only in SSO-enabled installations). For more information, see [User Identity](/run-ai/self-hosted/documentation/installation-and-configuration/configuration/security/user-identity-in-containers).

WorkingDir.description: Container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime default will be used. This may be configured in the container image.

InternalToolType.description: The type of the internal tool. Internal tool runs within the container and exposes ports associated with the tool using NodePort, LoadBalancer or ExternalUrl.

InternalConnectionType.description: The type of connection that exposes the container port.

isCustomPort.description: Whether the node port is provided in the specific env of the workspace. Default is false, and in this case the node port is auto generated by the system.

isCustomUrl.description: Whether external url is provided in the specific env of the workspace. Default is false, and in this case the external url is auto generated by the system.

externalUrl.description: Default value for the external url. You can override it in the specific env of the workspace. Should be specified for ExternalUrl only.

containerPort.description: The port within the container that the connection exposes.

ExternalToolType.description: The type of external tool that is associated with the connection. External tool typically runs in the cloud and require external url for connecting to it.

externalUrl.description: The external url for connecting to the external tool. The url can include environment variables that will be replaced with the value provided for those variables when the workspace is created.

name.description: A unique name of this connection. This name correlates between the connection information specified at the environment asset, to the information about the connection as specified in SpecificEnv for a specific workspace.

isExternal.description: Internal tools (isExternal=false) are tools that run as part of the container. External tools (isExternal=true) run outside the container, typically in the cloud.

connections.description: List of connections that either expose ports from the container (each port is associated with a tool that the container runs), or URL's to be used for connecting to an external tool that is related to the action of the container (such as Weights & Biases).

overrideUidGidInWorkspace.description: Allow specifying uid/gid as part of create workspace. This is relevant only for custom uigGidSource.

routingMethod.description: Indicates the supported routing method (host-base, path-base or agnostic)

HostPathMountPropagation.description: Share this volumes mount with other containers. If set to HostToContainer, this volume mount will receive all subsequent mounts that are mounted to this volume or any of its subdirectories. In case of multiple hostPath entries, this field should have the same value for all of them.

path.description: Local path within the controller to which the host volume will be mapped. (mandatory)

readOnly.description: Force the volume to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false.

mountPath.description: The path that the host volume will be mounted to when in use. (mandatory)

path.description: Path that is exported by the NFS server (mandatory). For more information, see [NFS](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#nfs).

readOnly.description: Force the NFS export to be mounted with read-only permissions.

server.description: The hostname or IP address of the NFS server. (mandatory)

mountPath.description: The path that the NFS volume will be mounted to when in use. (mandatory)

PvcClaimSize.description: Requested size for the PVC. Mandatory when existingPvc is false. Recommended sizes: TB/GB/MB/TIB/GIB/MIB

PvcAddedAttrValues.description: an optional array of key-values pairs that are written as annotations on the created PVC. the allowed attributes are determined according to the storage class configuration (see k8s-objects-tracker for further info).

path.description: Local path within the workload to which the PVC bucket will be mapped. (mandatory)

PvcAccessModes.description: Default access mode(s) applied to newly created PVCs unless explicitly overridden.

readWriteOnce.description: Mount the volume as read/write by a single node.

readOnlyMany.description: Mount the volume as read-only by many nodes.

readWriteMany.description: Mount the volume as read/write by many nodes.

PvcVolumeMode.description: Default volume mode for the PVC. Choose between Filesystem (default) or Block.

ClaimInfo.description: Claim information for the newly created PVC. The information should not be provided when attempting to use existing PVC.

storageClass.description: Storage class name to associate with the PVC. This parameter may be omitted if there is a single storage class in the system, or you are using the default storage class. For more information, see [Storage class](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/storage-classes).

existingPvc.description: Verify existing PVC. PVC is assumed to exist when set to `true`. If set to `false`, the PVC will be created, if it does not exist. Cannot be set to `true` when `dataSharing` is `true`.

claimName.description: Name for the PVC. Allow referencing it across workloads. If not provided, a name based on the workload name and scope will be auto-generated.

readOnly.description: Permit only read access to PVC.

ephemeral.description: Use `true` to set PVC to ephemeral. If set to `true`, the PVC will be deleted when the workload is stopped. Not supported for inference workloads.

dataSharing.description: Use `true` to share the PVC data to all projects under the selected scope. Cannot be set to `true` when `existingPvc` is `true`.

repository.description: URL to a remote Git repository. The content of this repository will be mapped to the container running the workload. (mandatory)

branch.description: Specific branch to synchronize the repository from.

revision.description: Specific revision to synchronize the repository from.

path.description: Local path within the workload to which the Git repository will be mapped (mandatory).

passwordAssetId.description: UUID of a credential asset of type userid / password. This credential is required for authenticating with private Git repositories using SSH. (deprecated - use credentialId instead).

credentialId.description: UUID of a credential asset of type generic secret or user id / password required for authenticating with private Git repositories. For generic secret, the credential asset must contain a key-value pair where the key is ssh (lowercase) and the value is a valid private SSH key

path.description: Local path within the workload to which the S3 bucket will be mapped. (mandatory)

url.description: The url of the S3 service provider. The default is the URL of the Amazon AWS S3 service.

accessKeyAssetId.description: ID of credentials asset of type access-key, for private S3 buckets.

DefaultMode.description: File permission mode in octal string format. This value must be a 4-digit octal number, representing the default file mode when mounting a Secret or ConfigMap as a volume.

configMap.description: The name of the ConfigMap resource. (mandatory)

mountPath.description: Local path within the workload to which the ConfigMap will be mapped to. (mandatory)

subPath.description: Path within the volume from which the container's volume should be mounted.

mountPath.description: Local path within the workspace to which the Secret will be mapped to (mandatory)

id.description: The unique identifier of the data volume. (mandatory)

originPvcName.description: The name of the PVC that the datavolume is based on

DatasourceRef.description: Reference information about a datasource asset.

AssetsRef.description: Reference information about a set of assets. used to describe - assets comprising a workspace - assets comprising a workspace template - assets that use other assets (e.g. s3 asset which uses access key).

name.description: Unique identifier of the connection. Will be used to correlate between the information given here and the information provided for the connection in the environment asset.

nodePort.description: Port number of the host that will be connected with the container port. Required if and only if isCustomPort is set to true in the environment asset.

externalUrl.description: URL to associated with the container port. Required if and only if isCustomExternalUrl is set to true in the environment asset.

authorizedUsers.description: List of users or applications that are allowed to access the URL. Note that authorizedUsers and authorizedGroups are mutually exclusive.

authorizedGroups.description: Specifies the names of those groups that are allowed to access the connection. Note that authorizedUsers and authorizedGroups are mutually exclusive.

Annotation.description: Annotation details to be populated into the container.

name.description: The name of the annotation (mandatory)

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the annotation is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

Annotations.description: Set of annotations to populate into the container running the workload.

AutoDeletionTimeAfterPreemption.description: Specifies the duration after which a finished workload (completed or failed) will be automatically deleted. The default is 30 days. Log retention is managed separately.

BackoffLimit.description: Specifies the number of retries before marking a workload as failed (not applicable to Inference workloads). The default value is 6.

Category.description: Specify the workload category assigned to the workload. Categories are used to classify and monitor different types of workloads within the NVIDIA Run:ai platform.

Completions.description: Used with Hyperparameter Optimization. Specifies the number of successful pods the job should reach to be completed. The Job will be marked as successful once the specified amount of pods has been reached (applicable to standard training only).

ImagePullSecret.description: A reference to a secret in the same namespace used to pull container images.

name.description: The name of the Kubernetes secret containing the image pull credentials.

userCredential.description: Indicates whether the secret is a user credential. Set to true if the secret was created by the user and is only accessible by them.

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the secret is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

ImagePullSecrets.description: A list of references to Kubernetes secrets in the same namespace used for pulling container images.

Label.description: Label details to be populated into the container.

name.description: The name of the label (mandatory)

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the label is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

Labels.description: Set of labels to populate into the container running the workload.

MatchExpressionOperator.description: Represents a key's relationship to a set of values (mandatory).

MatchExpression.description: A selector that contains values, a key, and an operator that relates the key and values.

key.description: The label key that the selector applies to (mandatory).

values.description: An array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty. If the operator is Gt or Lt, the values array must have a single element, which will be interpreted as an integer.

NodeSelectorTerm.description: A null or empty node selector term matches no objects. The requirements of them are ANDed.

matchExpressions.description: A list of node selector requirements by node's labels.

NodeAffinityRequired.description: If the affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node. If the affinity requirements specified by this field cease to be met at some point during pod execution (e.g. due to an update), the system may or may not try to eventually evict the pod from its node.

nodeSelectorTerms.description: A list of node selector terms. The terms are ORed.

NodePools.description: A prioritized list of node pools for the scheduler to run the workload on. The scheduler will always try to use the first node pool before moving to the next one if the first is not available.

NodeType.description: Deprecated: use a workload policy node selector to target node types instead. Nodes (machines), or a group of nodes on which the workload will run. To use this feature, your Administrator will need to label nodes. For more information, see [Group Nodes](https://docs.run.ai/latest/admin/researcher-setup/limit-to-node-group). When using this flag with with Project-based affinity, it refines the list of allowable node groups set in the Project. For more information, see [Projects](https://docshub.run.ai/guides/platform-management/aiinitiatives/organization/projects).

Parallelism.description: Used with Hyperparameter Optimization. Specifies the maximum number of pods the workload should run at any given time (applicable to standard training only).

PodAffinityType.description: The affinity type, required or preferred. (mandatory)

PodAffinity.description: Pod affinity scheduling rules (e.g. co-locate this workload in the same node, zone, etc. as some other workloads).

Preemptibility.description: Specifies whether the workload can be preempted by higher-priority workloads. Valid values are preemptible, semi-preemptible and non-preemptible. If explicitly set, this value takes precedence. If not set, the system derives the preemptibility from the priorityClassName field, ensuring backward compatibility. Each workload type has a default preemptibility. To view the default preemptibility for each workload type, use the GET /workload-types endpoint.

PriorityClass.description: Specifies the priority class for the workload, which determines its scheduling behavior. Valid values are: very-low, low, medium-low, medium, medium-high, high, and very-high. Each workload type has a default priority. To view the default priority for each workload type, use the GET /workload-types endpoint. Once you change the priority from the default value defined for that workload type, the preemptibility field is not automatically updated. Make sure to set the desired preemptibility value.

RestartPolicy.description:
Specify the restart policy of the workload pods. Default is empty, which is determine by the framework default.
The `Always` value is deprecated; use `OnFailure` or `Never` instead.

TerminateAfterPreemption.description: Indicates if the job should be terminated by the system after it has been preempted.

TerminationGracePeriod.description: Duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully upon probe failure. The grace period is the duration in seconds after the processes running in the pod are sent a termination signal and the time when the processes are forcibly halted with a kill signal. Set this value longer than the expected cleanup time for your process. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates stop immediately via the kill signal (no opportunity to shut down).

TolerationOperator.description: A key's relationship to the value. Equal uses key and value. Exists is equivalent to wildcard for value, so that a workload can tolerate all taints of a particular category. (mandatory)

name.description: The name of the toleration.

key.description: The taint key that the toleration applies to. (mandatory)

value.description: The taint value the toleration matches to. Mandatory if operator is Exists, forbidden otherwise.

seconds.description: The period of time the toleration tolerates the taint. Valid only if effect is NoExecute. taint.

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the label is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

Tolerations.description: Set of tolerations to apply to the workload.

allowOverQuota.description: Whether to allow the workload to exceed the quota of the project.

metricThresholdPercentage.description: The percentage of metric threshold value to use for autoscaling. Defaults to 70. Applicable only with the 'throughput' and 'concurrency' metrics

minReplicas.description: The minimum number of replicas for autoscaling. Defaults to 1. Use 0 to allow scale-to-zero

maxReplicas.description: The maximum number of replicas for autoscaling. Defaults to minReplicas, or to 1 if minReplicas is set to 0

initialReplicas.description: The number of replicas to run when initializing the workload for the first time. Defaults to minReplicas, or to 1 if minReplicas is set to 0

activationReplicas.description: The number of replicas to run when scaling-up from zero. Defaults to minReplicas, or to 1 if minReplicas is set to 0

concurrencyHardLimit.description: The maximum number of requests allowed to flow to a single replica at any time. 0 means no limit

scaleToZeroRetentionSeconds.description: The minimum amount of time (in seconds) that the last replica will remain active after a scale-to-zero decision. Defaults to 0. Available only if minReplicas is set to 0

scaleDownDelaySeconds.description: The minimum amount of time (in seconds) that a replica will remain active after a scale-down decision

initializationTimeoutSeconds.description: Use `servingConfiguration.initializationTimeoutSeconds` instead.  If this field is set, it will be ignored and the value under `servingConfiguration` will be used. The maximum amount of time (in seconds) to wait for the container to become ready.

AutoScalingMetric.description: The metric to use for autoscaling. Mandatory if minReplicas < maxReplicas, except for the special case where minReplicas is set to 0 and maxReplicas is set to 1, as in this case autoscaling decisions are made according to network activity rather than metrics. Use one of the built-in metrics of 'throughput', 'concurrency' or 'latency', or any other available custom metric. Only the 'throughput' and 'concurrency' metrics support scale-to-zero

thresholdValue.description: The threshold value to use with the specified metric for autoscaling

ServingPortAccessAuthorizationTypeEnum.description:
Specifies who can send inference requests to the serving endpoint:

Possible values:
- `public`: No authorization is required. (Default)
- `authenticatedUsers`: Any NVIDIA Run:ai authenticated user and service account can send requests.
- `authorizedUsers`: Only users listed in the authorizedUsers field can send requests.
- `authorizedGroups`: Only members of user groups listed in the authorizedGroups field can send requests.
- `authorizedUsersOrGroups`: Requires either authorizedUsers or authorizedGroups to be provided; if neither is set, or if both are set, a mutual exclusion error is reported. Supported from cluster version 2.19.

AuthorizedUsers.description: List of users or service accounts that are allowed to access the URL. Note that authorizedUsers and authorizedGroups are mutually exclusive.

clusterLocalAccessOnly.description: Configure the serving port URL to be available only on the cluster-local network, and not externally. Defaults to false

Determines the behavior when a pod fails.
- `RecreateGroupOnPodRestart`: Restarts all pods in the group if any pod fails.
- `None`: No automatic restart behavior is applied.

DistributedInferenceServingPortAccessAut.description:
Specifies who can send inference requests to the serving endpoint:

Possible values:
- `public`: No authorization is required. (Default)
- `authenticatedUsers`: Any NVIDIA Run:ai authenticated user and service account can send requests.
- `authorizedUsers`: Only users listed in the authorizedUsers field can send requests.
- `authorizedGroups`: Only members of user groups listed in the authorizedGroups field can send requests.

authorizedUsers.description: A list of users and service accounts allowed to send inference requests to the serving endpoint. `Note:` Cannot be used together with authorizedGroups.

authorizedGroups.description: A list of user groups allowed to send inference requests to the serving endpoint. `Note:` Cannot be used together with authorizedUsers.

exposeExternally.description: Indicates whether the inference serving endpoint should be accessible outside the cluster. If set to true, the endpoint will be exposed externally. To enable external access, your administrator must configure the cluster as described in the [inference requirements](/run-ai/self-hosted/documentation/installation-and-configuration/system-requirements/networking-setup#standard-inference-wildcard-certificate). section.

exposedUrl.description: The custom URL to use for the serving port. If empty (default), an autogenerated URL will be used.

DistributedInferenceServingPort.description: Defines the configuration for the inference serving endpoint. This determines how applications or services can send inference requests to the workload.

DistributedInferenceStartupPolicy.description:
Determines when the worker pods should start during workload initialization. 
 - `LeaderCreated`: Workers start after the leader pod is created.
 - `LeaderReady`: Workers start only after the leader pod is ready.

workers.description: Specifies the number of worker nodes to run. If set to 0, only the leader node will run, and no worker pods will be created. In this case, worker spec is not required.

replicas.description:
Specifies the number of leader-worker sets to deploy. Each replica represents a group consisting of one leader pod and multiple worker pods. 
For example, setting replicas: 3 will create 3 independent groups, each with its own leader and corresponding set of workers.

metricThreshold.description: The threshold to use with the specified metric for autoscaling. Mandatory if metric is specified

initializationTimeoutSeconds.description: The maximum time (in seconds) allowed for a workload to initialize and become ready. If the workload does not start within this time, it will be moved to failed state.

requestTimeoutSeconds.description: The maximum time (in seconds) allowed to process an end-user request. If no response is returned within this time, the request will be ignored.Supported from Cluster version 2.22

CleanPodPolicy.description: The policy describes how to deal with pods when the job is finished.

Url.description: The URL for connecting to the container port. If not specified, the URL will be auto-generated by the system.

AuthorizationType.description:
Specifies who can access the connection URL:
- `authenticatedUsers`: Any authenticated user or service account can access the URL; the authorizedUsers and authorizedGroups fields are ignored.
- `authorizedUsers`: Only users listed in the authorizedUsers field are allowed to access the URL; the authorizedGroups field is ignored.
- `authorizedGroups`: Only members of user groups listed in the authorizedGroups field are allowed to access the URL; the authorizedUsers field is ignored.
If not specified, authorization is determined by whether authorizedUsers or authorizedGroups is present. If both fields are set, this results in an error. If neither is set, any authenticatedUser can access.

toolName.description: A name describing the tool that runs on this url.

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the instance is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

ExposedUrls.description: Set of container ports that the workload exposes via URLs.

MinReplicas.description: the lower limit for the number of worker pods to which the training job can scale down. (applicable only for PyTorch)

MpiLauncherCreationPolicy.description: Define whether the MPI Launcher is created in parallel with the workers, or if its creation is postponed until all workers are in  Ready state. This prevents failures when the launcher attempts to connect to workers that are not yet ready.

NumWorkers.description: the number of workers that will be allocated for running the workload.

PortServiceType.description: The service type of the port (mandatory).

Port.description: A port for accessing the workload.

container.description: The port that the container running the workload exposes. (mandatory)

external.description: The external port which allows a connection to the container port. If not specified, the port will be auto-generated by the system..

toolType.description: The tool type that runs on this port.

toolName.description: A name describing the tool that runs on this port.

name.description: Unique name to identify the instance. primarily used for policy locked rules.

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the item is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

Ports.description: Set of container ports that the workload exposes.

RelatedUrl.description: A URL that is related to the workload. For example, a URL to an external server providing statistics or logging about the workload.

url.description: The URL for connecting an external service related to the workload. (mandatory)

type.description: The type of service that the url provides. For example, wandb (Weights & Biases). (mandatory)

name.description: Unique name to identify the instance. primarily used for policy locked rules.

exclude.description: Use 'true' in case the item is defined in defaults of the policy, and you wish to exclude it from the workload.

RelatedUrls.description: Set of URLs that are related to the workload.

SegmentSize.description:
The number of workers per topology segment.
Workers in the same segment will be placed on nodes that are as close as possible, reducing latency between them.
Set this to match your application's parallel segment size.
Omit this field to disable segmentation.

SlotsPerWorker.description: Specifies the number of slots per worker used in hostfile. Defaults to 1. (applicable only for MPI)

SshAuthMountPath.description: Specifies the directory where SSH keys are mounted. (applicable only for MPI)

DataVolumeItems.description: Set of data volumes to use in the workload.

passwordSecret.description: Secret containing the credentials of the repository (needed for non public repository which requires authentication). (deprecated)

secretKeyOfUser.description: The key to use for loading the user name from the secret. The default is `User`. (deprecated)

secretKeyOfPassword.description: The key to use for loading the password from the secret. The default is `Password`. (deprecated)

GitAuthenticationMethod.description: Specifies the authentication method to use when accessing the Git repository. This is required for private repositories - `password` - Authenticate using a username and password. - `ssh-key` - Authenticate using an SSH private key.

name.description: Name of the Secret containing the credentials of the repository.

secretKeyOfUser.description: The key in the Secret that contains the Git username (used for `password` authentication).

secretKeyOfPassword.description: The key in the Secret that contains the Git password (used for `password` authentication).

GitItems.description: Set of git repositories to use in the workload.

HostPathItems.description: Set of host paths to use in the workload.

NfsItems.description: Set of nfs volumes to use in the workload.

accessKeySecret.description: Name of the secret containing credentials of the S3 bucket. Used for private S3 buckets.

secretKeyOfAccessKeyId.description: The key to use for loading the access key id from the secret. The default is `AccessKeyId`. For more information, see [Credentials access keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html).

secretKeyOfSecretKey.description: The key to use for loading the secret key from the secret. The default is `SecretKey`. For more information, see [Credentials access keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html).

awsSessionToken.description: An AWS session token. It should be provided (in addition to the access key ID and secret access key) to authenticate to a bucket that is configured to use AWS Security Token Service (STS).

S3Items.description: Set of s3 buckets to use in the workload.

AutoDeletionTimeAfterPreemptionMaster.description: Specifies the duration after which a finished workload (completed or failed) will be automatically deleted. The default is 30 days. Log retention is managed separately.

BackoffLimitMaster.description: Specifies the number of retries before marking a workload as failed (not applicable to Inference workloads). The default value is 6.

PriorityClassMaster.description: Specifies the priority class for the workload, which determines its scheduling behavior. Valid values are: very-low, low, medium-low, medium, medium-high, high, and very-high. Each workload type has a default priority. To view the default priority for each workload type, use the GET /workload-types endpoint. Once you change the priority from the default value defined for that workload type, the preemptibility field is not automatically updated. Make sure to set the desired preemptibility value.

TerminationGracePeriodMaster.description: Duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully upon probe failure. The grace period is the duration in seconds after the processes running in the pod are sent a termination signal and the time when the processes are forcibly halted with a kill signal. Set this value longer than the expected cleanup time for your process. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates stop immediately via the kill signal (no opportunity to shut down).

AssetFlatResponse.description: flat representation of an asset, for a given project and workload type

ServingPortProtocol.description: The protocol used by the port, defaults to http

AssetScopeFilter.name: scope
AssetScopeFilter.description: Filters results by scope. Returns only assets that belong to the specified scope. Mutually exclusive with includeDescendants. Valid values: tenant, cluster, department, project.

AssetProjectFilter.name: projectId
AssetProjectFilter.description: Filter results by project id. If scope filter is project, only assets from the specific project will be included in the response. Otherwise, the response will include project, department, cluster, tenant and system assets.

FilterByCluster.name: clusterId
FilterByCluster.description: Filter using the Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) of the cluster.

IncludeUsageInfo.name: usageInfo
IncludeUsageInfo.description: Whether the query should include asset usage information as part of the response.

ComplyToProject.name: complyToProject
ComplyToProject.description: Include workload creation compliance information of an asset, for a given project, as part of the response. To check compliance, you need to provide both project id and workload type.

ComplyToWorkloadType.name: complyToWorkloadType
ComplyToWorkloadType.description: Include workload creation compliance information of an asset, for a given workload type, as part of the response. To check compliance, you need to provide both project id and workload type.

EnvironmentId.name: environmentId
EnvironmentId.description: The id of the environment to which the asset belongs.

ComplyToReplicaType.name: complyToReplicaType
ComplyToReplicaType.description: Include workload creation compliance information of an asset, for a given replica type, as part of the response. To check compliance, you need to provide both project id and workload type. For distributed, replica type should be provided as well.

AssetDepartmentFilter.name: departmentId
AssetDepartmentFilter.description: Filter results by department id. If scope filter is department, only assets from the specific department will be included in the response. Otherwise, the response will include department, cluster, tenant and system assets.

AssetClusterFilter.name: clusterId
AssetClusterFilter.description: Filter results by Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) of the cluster. If scope filter is cluster, only assets from the specific cluster will be included in the response. Otherwise, the response will include cluster, tenant and system assets.

includeDescendants.name: includeDescendants
includeDescendants.description: Indicates whether to include assets from all descendant scopes under the specified scope. When set to true, and a specific scope identifier (for example, clusterId) is provided, the query also returns assets from all nested scopes within it (for example, departments and projects).  Mutually exclusive with scope.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: The offset of the first item returned in the collection.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: The maximum number of entries to return.

SortOrder.name: sortOrder
SortOrder.description: Sort results in descending or ascending order.

RctsFilter.name: filterBy
RctsFilter.description: Filter results by a parameter. Use the format field-name operator value. Operators are `==` Equals, `!=` Not equals, `<=` Less than or equal, `>=` Greater than or equal, `=@` contains, `!@` Does not contain, `=^` Starts with and `=$` Ends with. Dates are in ISO 8601 timestamp format and available for operators `==`, `!=`, `<=` and `>=`. At most one scope anchor (clusterId, departmentId or projectId) may be provided. The anchor is combined with includeAncestors / includeDescendants to determine which scopes of the hierarchy are returned.

IncludeAncestors.name: includeAncestors
IncludeAncestors.description: When a scope anchor (clusterId, departmentId or projectId) is provided, set includeAncestors=true to also include resource claim templates from the anchor's ancestor scopes (for example, for a project: its parent department and cluster, as well as tenant and system scoped templates). Defaults to true to preserve the backward-compatible scope-usability behavior.

IncludeStatus.name: statusInfo
IncludeStatus.description: Whether the query should include asset status information as part of the response.

SyncAfter.name: after
SyncAfter.description: search for updates with update counter greater than the value passed for this parameter

PrivateOnly.name: privateOnly
PrivateOnly.description: Whether the query should include private assets. mutually exclusive with `includePrivate` parameter.

IncludePrivate.name: includePrivate
IncludePrivate.description: Whether the query should include private assets. mutually exclusive with `privateOnly` parameter.

CredentialsTypeFilter.name: type
CredentialsTypeFilter.description: Filter credentials by type. If provided, only credentials of the specified type will be returned.

DistributedFrameworkQuery.name: distributedFramework

IsDistributedInferenceQuery.name: isDistributedInference
IsDistributedInferenceQuery.description: Filter results to workload of type distributed inference.

AssetIdsFilter.name: assetIds

IncludeDataVolumes.name: dataVolumes
IncludeDataVolumes.description: Whether the query should include data volumes

DatasourceTypeFilter.name: type
DatasourceTypeFilter.description: Filter datasources by type. If provided, only datasources of the specified type will be returned.

IncludeDVUsageInfo.name: dvUsageInfo
IncludeDVUsageInfo.description: Whether the query should include data volume usage information as part of the response.
